2992.takeaway: A partnership milestone shaped by clients, colleagues and the wider Frappe community.

sections.heading: Recognition across Africa
paragraphs: Navari received the Frappe Partner Award 2026 for partnerships in the Africa region during the partner meetup in Mumbai. The recognition marks a shared milestone for the company and the organisations it works with.

sections.heading: The work behind the recognition
paragraphs: Navari’s announcement connects the award to its everyday priorities: understanding customer needs, solving operational problems and improving delivery. It also acknowledges the contribution of clients, the team and the Frappe community.

sections.heading: Looking ahead
paragraphs: The announcement closes with a commitment to keep learning and improving. Read Navari’s original publication for the team’s own words about the award.

2771.takeaway: Build carefully, take ownership and grow alongside the community.

sections.heading: Roots in Meru
paragraphs: Muchai Gateru’s journey begins in Meru, where his parents and local entrepreneurs shaped his approach to work. Their influence runs through the company story: take responsibility, understand your capacity and do the work well.

sections.heading: Finding the right foundation
paragraphs: After a career in software development and Microsoft Dynamics, Muchai founded Navari in 2015. Integration challenges on a healthcare project later strengthened his interest in a connected platform, leading the business towards ERPNext and Frappe.

sections.heading: Growing with purpose
paragraphs: The published profile describes a company built through persistence, careful project selection and investment in its people. Community events and contributions such as local compliance and M-Pesa integrations form part of that approach.
The complete profile follows this journey in greater depth, including Muchai’s reflections and photographs from the Navari community.

2516.takeaway: Evaluate the fit between your processes, your implementation partner and the platform.

sections.heading: Start with the operating challenges
paragraphs: Navari’s article considers the problems businesses face when information is fragmented: limited visibility, manual work and disconnected departments. Those needs provide a practical starting point for evaluating an ERP system.

sections.heading: Consider the platform and its flexibility
paragraphs: The article highlights ERPNext’s connected business functions and open-source foundation. It also discusses adapting systems to regional requirements and supporting teams across locations.

sections.heading: Plan for implementation
paragraphs: Local consulting, configuration and support matter alongside product selection. A suitable implementation needs to address the organisation’s workflows and operating context, rather than treating software selection as the final step.
Read the original article for Navari’s broader perspective on ERPNext in East Africa.

2514.takeaway: Connected information is most useful when the system fits the organisation using it.

sections.heading: A connected view of the business
paragraphs: Navari’s article explores the interest in integrated business software across African organisations. ERPNext brings functions such as finance, inventory and manufacturing into a shared operational foundation.

sections.heading: Room to adapt
paragraphs: The open-source model and configurable workflows are central to the article’s argument. It considers regional requirements and the different infrastructure needs of growing organisations, including cloud and on-premise deployment.

sections.heading: Support beyond the software
paragraphs: The article also points to the role of local partners and the wider community in implementation and training. Its focus is the combination of flexible software and practical support for the people who use it.
The original publication expands on these themes and Navari’s perspective on ERP adoption in Africa.

2275.takeaway: The right implementation connects processes, visibility and responsibility.

media.label: Ciira Agrovet Supplies Limited — full case study

sections.heading: The distribution challenge
paragraphs: Ciira Agrovet Supplies Limited’s presentation describes an agricultural-input distribution business working across branches, suppliers and customers. Its story examines the operational challenges behind the move towards a more structured system.

sections.heading: Connecting the operation
paragraphs: The case study discusses inventory control, branch visibility, supplier management and workflows. It presents implementation quality, ownership and accountability as important parts of making ERPNext useful in daily work.

sections.heading: The implementation journey
paragraphs: Data migration, user adoption and change management feature among the challenges covered in the presentation. The full document provides the customer’s account of the journey and its reported outcomes.
Open the original twelve-page presentation below to explore the complete case study.

2257.takeaway: A customer's perspective on choosing an ERP and putting it to work.

sections.heading: Connecting separate systems
paragraphs: Amotech Africa’s presentation describes a business seeking to connect its customer, finance and people processes. Its search began with CRM requirements and expanded into a wider ERP evaluation as integration challenges became clearer.

sections.heading: Finding the right fit
paragraphs: The customer account identifies integration, flexibility, cost and support for regional growth as important selection criteria. A demonstration arranged with Navari introduced ERPNext as an option for the company’s evolving needs.

sections.heading: The experience in practice
paragraphs: The presentation reports a move towards shared departmental workflows, fewer disconnected tools and continued learning as the system came into everyday use. These are the customer’s observations from the time of publication.

1852.takeaway: Explore the relationship between the platform, its partners and customer delivery.

254.takeaway: A shared system can connect work from farmer registration to the finished product.

sections.heading: From farms to finished products
paragraphs: Meru Greens Horticulture works with smallholder farmers to produce and market fruit and vegetables. Navari’s case study follows the processes behind its vegetable packaging operation, from planting inputs to production and distribution.

sections.heading: Bringing the information together
paragraphs: The original story describes fragmented farmer information, stock challenges and limited reporting. The implementation connects farmer records, purchasing, selling, production and inventory, using configuration and targeted customization.

sections.heading: Making the transition
paragraphs: The published account covers process mapping, migration, training, acceptance testing and support after launch. It also highlights the importance of a customer-side project champion and clear coordination.
Read the complete original case study for the detailed workflows and the implementation context at the time of publication.
